headline: The US stock market's four-year bull run, up 117%, now depends heavily on AI spending, and Reuters says rising interest rates and Treasury yields are the main risks.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: a useful market-context piece; facts support the headline, but it is analysis, not a new event.
importance_line: What changed is a timely check on how much of the market's rise rests on AI, which matters first to savers and pension holders in US shares, then to investors weighing a rate-hike cycle, and the doubt is that strategists differ on whether the bull market is about to end.
summary: Reuters reports that the S&P 500 is trading near record highs as it nears four years since its October 2022 low, a rise of 117% driven by AI spending that has lifted corporate profits, with the Federal Reserve's recent rate rises, a 10-year Treasury yield near 5.2% and heavy reliance on AI stocks cited as risks. The top 10 companies now make up about 40% of the index, up from about 28% in October 2022, and Ameriprise strategist Anthony Saglimbene says "the easy money around AI has been made".
notes: Read through The Globe and Mail, which republishes the Reuters article; the Reuters link in the pool is the original.
